items.followUp: Differentiate between translatory and rotatory motion.

rubric.why: Shows that rotatory motion is motion around an axis.
rubric.description: Identifies rotatory motion as motion about an axis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a body rotates about an axis or that its points move in circular paths around the axis.

rubric.why: Distinguishes vibration from rotation by its back-and-forth motion around a central position.
rubric.description: Identifies vibratory motion as to-and-fro motion about a mean position.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the motion as to and fro, or oscillatory, about a mean or equilibrium position.

modelAnswer: Rotatory motion: Motion of a body about an axis; its points move in circular paths around that axis.
Vibratory motion: To-and-fro motion of a body about its mean position.

items.followUp: Define circular motion and give one example.

rubric.why: Explains the defining feature of random motion.
rubric.description: Defines random motion as motion with no fixed path or direction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for saying the motion is irregular, unpredictable, or has no fixed path or direction.

rubric.why: Provides a valid example of random motion.
rubric.description: Gives an example of random motion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a suitable example, such as gas molecules or a flying mosquito.

modelAnswer: Random motion is motion in which an object moves irregularly, without a fixed path or direction.
Example: The random motion of gas molecules.

items.followUp: What is friction? State one factor that affects its magnitude.

rubric.why: States the direction of friction relative to the motion it resists.
rubric.description: States that friction acts opposite to motion or relative motion.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that friction opposes the motion or relative motion of surfaces.

rubric.why: Explains the cause of the opposing force between surfaces.
rubric.description: Explains that surface irregularities interlock and resist sliding.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that the irregularities of surfaces in contact interlock and resist their relative motion.

modelAnswer: Friction acts opposite to the motion or relative motion of surfaces in contact.
The irregularities of the surfaces interlock and resist sliding, so friction opposes motion.

rubric.why: Identifies damage caused by friction between surfaces.
rubric.description: Gives wear or damage to surfaces as a disadvantage of friction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that friction causes wear and tear or damages moving surfaces.

rubric.why: Identifies energy loss or reduced efficiency caused by friction.
rubric.description: Gives heat production or energy loss as a disadvantage of friction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that friction produces unwanted heat, wastes energy, or reduces efficiency.

modelAnswer: Friction causes wear and tear of moving parts.
Friction produces unwanted heat and wastes energy, reducing the efficiency of machines.

items.followUp: What is an ideal rigid body?

rubric.why: States that a rigid body does not deform.
rubric.description: States that the shape and size of a rigid body remain unchanged when a force is applied.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for saying that its shape or size does not change under an applied force.

rubric.why: Gives the defining condition for an ideal rigid body.
rubric.description: States that the distance between any two particles of the body remains constant.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the separation between any two points or particles remains constant.

modelAnswer: A rigid body is an ideal body whose shape and size do not change when a force is applied.
The distance between any two points of a rigid body remains constant.

items.followUp: State the second condition of equilibrium.

rubric.why: States the force condition required for equilibrium.
rubric.description: States that the resultant force on the body is zero.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving zero resultant or net force, or the equivalent equation.

rubric.why: Connects the condition to translational equilibrium or its consequence.
rubric.description: Identifies this as the condition for translational equilibrium, with zero linear acceleration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming translational equilibrium or stating that the body has no linear acceleration.

modelAnswer: The first condition of equilibrium is that the resultant force on a body is zero: ΣF = 0.
This condition is called translational equilibrium; the body has no linear acceleration.

items.followUp: Give one example of a field force and explain why it is called a field force.

rubric.why: Distinguishes a field force from a contact force.
rubric.description: States that a field force acts without physical contact between bodies.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for saying the force acts without contact or at a distance.

rubric.why: Provides a valid example of a force that acts through a field.
rubric.description: Gives a valid example of a field force.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming gravitational, magnetic, or electric force.

modelAnswer: A field force acts on a body without physical contact, through a field.
Examples include gravitational, magnetic, and electric forces.

items.followUp: Define kinetic energy and write its equation.

rubric.why: Defines potential energy in terms of position or configuration.
rubric.description: Defines potential energy as energy due to a body's position or configuration.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking potential energy to position or configuration.

rubric.why: Gives the required equation for gravitational potential energy.
rubric.description: Writes the equation for gravitational potential energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for writing PE = mgh or an equivalent notation.

modelAnswer: Potential energy is the energy possessed by a body due to its position or configuration.
For gravitational potential energy: PE = mgh, where m is mass, g is gravitational acceleration, and h is height.
